newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Israel regrets refusal to cooperate on environment.
newsitem.headline: Israel regrets refusal to cooperate on environment.

text.p: Israel expressed regret (on) Wednesday that some of its neighbours had refused to join in regional efforts to protect the environment.

"To our great regret, we have yet to tap the full potential for cooperation with our closest neighbours," Israeli U.N. envoy David Peleg told an Earth Summit reviewing progress since a 1992 environment conference in Rio de Janeiro.

"The multilateral track of the Middle East peace process, designed to identify and define joint developmental needs... is not functioning effectively, due to the refusal of some of our neighbours to participate therein and the intent of others to use this track as a platform for pressuring Israel," he said.

"We must understand that peace and the environment are interdependent. The move toward cooperative relations and mutual trust between the peoples of the region is of benefit to the environment. Peace will make it possible to establish regional frameworks, to preserve joint resources and to create new ones."

Peleg said a recently completed joint research project between Israel, Jordan and Palestinians in the most arid sections of the Dead Sea and Arava area represented a good example of collaboration and the potential for development throughout the entire region.
He said Israel for more than 40 years had acted to share its experience and learn from others in such fields as solar energy and the recycling of urban and industrial waste water.
"Last year alone, over 4,000 trainees from around the globe participated in our annual courses conducted in nine different languages," he said.
